abrupt.ex: The meeting came to an abrupt end.

accommodated.ex: The refugees were accommodated in a local hotel.

example.zh: 這家飯店最多可容納兩百位客人。

note.meaning: 為…提供住處；安置。文中指讓租戶能較快住進房屋。
note.usage: 常見 accommodate sb（安置某人）；也可指「容納」或「配合需求」：accommodate needs/requests。

noteEn.meaning: to give someone a place to live or stay; to have room for.

noteHi.exampleTr: होटल में 200 मेहमानों तक को ठहराया जा सकता है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी को रहने की जगह देना; ठहराना या समायोजित करना।
noteHi.usage: accommodate sb; accommodate needs/requests (ज़रूरतें पूरी करना) आम हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: そのホテルは最大200人の客を収容できる。
noteJa.meaning: （人に）住居を提供する、収容する。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 호텔은 최대 200명의 손님을 수용할 수 있다.
noteKo.usage: accommodate sb, accommodate needs(요구를 수용하다)로도 쓴다.

accommodation.en: a place to live or stay
accommodation.ex: The college offers accommodation to first-year students.

acquire.ex: The museum hopes to acquire two new paintings.

acquiring.ex: They are acquiring land for a new school.

note.meaning: 取得；收購。文中指地方政府從開發商購入新建房屋的交易。
note.usage: 可數名詞：make an acquisition；也常見 land/property acquisition、the acquisition of sth。

noteEs.usage: Se usa como the acquisition of algo; property/land acquisition.

noteHi.exampleTr: ज़मीन के अधिग्रहण में दो साल लगे।
noteHi.meaning: कुछ खरीदकर या पाकर अपने पास लाना; अधिग्रहण।
noteHi.usage: the acquisition of sth; property/land acquisition आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: その土地の取得には2年かかった。
noteJa.usage: the acquisition of ～、property acquisition の形でよく使う。

noteKo.usage: the acquisition of ~, property acquisition 형태로 자주 쓴다.

acquisitions.ex: The library made several new acquisitions this year.

example.zh: 取得這塊土地花了兩年時間。

note.meaning: 取得；收購。文中指地方政府從開發商購入新建房屋的交易。
note.usage: 可數名詞：make an acquisition；也常見 land/property acquisition、the acquisition of sth。

noteEn.meaning: the act of getting or buying something, such as property or a company.

noteHi.meaning: कुछ खरीदकर या पाकर अपने पास लाना; अधिग्रहण।
noteHi.usage: the acquisition of sth; property/land acquisition आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.usage: the acquisition of ～、property acquisition の形でよく使う。

noteKo.usage: the acquisition of ~, property acquisition 형태로 자주 쓴다.

note.usage: 常用 be contingent on/upon sth；名詞 contingency 指「意外狀況、應變」。

noteHi.usage: be contingent on/upon sth आम प्रयोग है।

noteKo.usage: be contingent on/upon ~ 형태로 자주 쓴다.

developers.ex: Developers plan to build flats on the old site.

diminishing.ex: Rising prices are diminishing people's savings.

example.en: The noise diminished as the train moved away.
example.zh: 火車開遠後，噪音逐漸減弱。

note.meaning: 減少；削弱。文中指此做法減少了可供自住買家購買的房屋存量。
note.usage: 可作及物或不及物：diminish the supply（使減少）/ sth diminishes（變少）；常見 diminishing returns。

noteEn.meaning: to become or make something smaller or less.

noteEs.exampleTr: El ruido disminuyó a medida que el tren se alejaba.
noteEs.usage: Puede ser transitivo o intransitivo: diminish the value; diminishing returns.

noteHi.exampleTr: ट्रेन के दूर जाने पर शोर कम हो गया।
noteHi.meaning: कम करना या कम होना; घटाना।
noteHi.usage: diminish the supply/value; diminishing returns आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 電車が遠ざかるにつれて騒音は小さくなった。
noteJa.meaning: 減らす、減少する、弱まる。
noteJa.usage: 他動詞・自動詞の両方。diminish the value、diminishing returns（収穫逓減）。

noteKo.usage: 타동사·자동사 모두 가능. diminish the value, diminishing returns.

direct.ex: The flood was a direct result of the storm.

directly.ex: You can buy tickets directly from the theatre.

discontinue.ex: The shop will discontinue this model next month.

example.zh: 這家公司明年將停產這款型號。

note.meaning: 停止；中止（某做法、服務或產品）。文中指政府打算停止地方政府購買「交鑰匙」房屋。

noteHi.meaning: किसी काम, सेवा या उत्पाद को बंद करना।

noteJa.meaning: （慣行・サービス・製品を）中止する、打ち切る。
noteJa.usage: 改まった語。discontinue a service、be discontinued（製造中止）の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 회사는 내년에 이 모델을 단종할 것이다.

diverts.en: sends something in a different direction

example.zh: 市政府把經費從道路轉用於學校。

note.meaning: 轉移；使改變方向或用途。文中指此做法把房屋從私人市場轉走。
note.usage: 常用 divert sth (away) from A to B；也可指 divert attention（轉移注意力）、divert traffic（改道）。

noteEs.exampleTr: La ciudad desvió dinero de las carreteras a las escuelas.
noteEs.meaning: Desviar; cambiar la dirección o el uso de algo.
noteEs.usage: divert algo from A to B; divert attention/traffic.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर ने सड़कों का पैसा स्कूलों की ओर मोड़ दिया।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ की दिशा या उपयोग बदल देना; मोड़ना।
noteHi.usage: divert sth from A to B; divert attention/traffic आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 市は道路の予算を学校に回した。
noteJa.meaning: （方向・用途を）そらす、転用する。

noteKo.usage: divert ~ from A to B, divert attention(주의를 돌리다).

noteHi.exampleTr: माता-पिता अक्सर अपने बच्चों पर गहरा प्रभाव डालते हैं।
noteHi.usage: exert influence/pressure/control on/over sth आम हैं।

noteJa.usage: exert influence/pressure/control on/over ～ の形で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 부모는 흔히 자녀에게 큰 영향을 미친다.

gradual.ex: There has been a gradual rise in prices.

greater.ex: Teachers want greater support from parents.

have.en: to own or hold; also helps form tenses

homes.ex: New homes are being built near the river.

hopes.ex: She hopes to visit Japan next year.

noteHi.exampleTr: टीम ने ऐप में धीरे-धीरे सुधार किए।
noteHi.meaning: धीरे-धीरे, छोटे-छोटे चरणों में होने वाला।

noteKo.usage: incremental change/increase로 자주 쓴다. 부사는 incrementally.

influence.en: to have an effect on something

involve.ex: The job involves a lot of travel.

kind.ex: What kind of music do you like?

land.ex: They bought land to build a farm.

leaves.en: causes someone to be in a situation

lists.ex: Write your name on the waiting list.

local.en: in or from a nearby area

low.ex: Many families on low pay struggle with rent.

maintains.ex: He maintains that the plan will work.

market.en: the buying and selling of homes

marks.en: is a sign of an important change

means.ex: The bike is her main means of transport.

mechanism.ex: The fund is a mechanism for helping poor areas.

minister.en: a leader of a government department

model.en: a system or way of doing something

moment.ex: She is busy at the moment.

noteHi.exampleTr: बिक्री बढ़ने से बढ़ती लागत की भरपाई हुई।
noteHi.meaning: किसी नुकसान या असर की भरपाई करना; संतुलित करना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 売上の増加が上昇するコストの埋め合わせになった。

outspoken.ex: She is an outspoken critic of the new tax.

permissible.ex: Phones are not permissible during the exam.

place.ex: She went to the meeting in place of her boss.

paragraphs: The Government is changing how councils get homes for people on low incomes.
Today, councils often buy new homes from builders. These are called turnkey homes. The homes are ready, so people can move in fast.
But the Housing Minister, James Browne, wants this to stop. He says these homes could go to people who want to buy a home. He also says the State cannot choose what kind of homes it gets.
The plan went to the Cabinet on Tuesday. Councils can ask to buy turnkey homes until 31 December 2027. Then it will stop.
After that, councils and housing groups will build more homes themselves. The Land Development Agency, a State body, will also build more homes.
The Government has decided that local councils will stop buying ready-made turnkey homes for social housing. The plan was brought to the Cabinet on Tuesday by the Minister for Housing, James Browne.

Social housing is housing for people who cannot afford to rent or buy a home on the private market. Councils and housing charities provide these homes at a lower rent. Buying turnkey homes has been one way for councils to get more of them.

At the moment, councils often buy new homes from private builders when the homes are finished. The homes are then given to families on social housing lists. This is a quick way to get homes, but it has been criticised.
Mr Browne has said that these sales take homes away from people who want to buy their own home. He has strongly criticised councils for buying homes that could have been sold on the open market.
He also believes that the State has no real say in what kind of homes are built when it buys them this way. For example, it cannot decide the size or type of the homes.
The change will not happen immediately. Councils can still apply to buy turnkey homes until 31 December 2027. After that date, the scheme will end.

Instead, the Government wants councils, approved housing bodies and the Land Development Agency to build more social homes themselves. Mr Browne hopes this will give the State more control over the homes it provides.
The Government is to end the practice of local authorities buying so-called turnkey homes for social housing, under a measure brought to Cabinet on Tuesday by the Minister for Housing, James Browne.

Social housing is provided by local authorities and not-for-profit housing bodies to households that cannot afford private rents. Buying finished homes from developers has been one of the ways councils have increased the number of social homes they can offer.

Turnkey homes are newly built properties that councils purchase from developers once construction is complete. They allow local authorities to house people quickly, but the approach has been blamed for reducing the number of homes available to private buyers.

Mr Browne has been highly critical of councils acquiring homes that would otherwise have been sold on the private market. He also argues that the State has little opportunity to influence the types of units it receives under these deals, such as their size or design.
The change will not take effect straight away. The final date for councils to submit applications for turnkey purchases will be 31 December 2027.

In place of turnkey purchases, the Government intends to expand building programmes run directly by local authorities, approved housing bodies and the Land Development Agency, the State's housing developer.

The decision marks a significant shift in housing policy. The minister believes that building homes directly will give the State greater control over the size, type and location of social housing, while leaving more new homes for buyers on the private market.

The Government is set to call time on local authorities purchasing so-called turnkey homes for social housing, following a proposal brought before Cabinet on Tuesday by the Minister for Housing, James Browne.

Social housing, let at below-market rents to households unable to afford private accommodation, is delivered by councils and not-for-profit approved housing bodies. Turnkey deals have offered councils a convenient route to bolstering their stock without shouldering the risks of construction themselves.

Under the turnkey model, councils acquire newly completed homes directly from developers, enabling them to house tenants with minimal delay. Critics, however, contend that the practice has crowded out private purchasers at a time when supply remains acutely constrained.

Mr Browne has been outspoken in his criticism of councils snapping up properties that would otherwise have reached the open market. He also maintains that the arrangement leaves the State with scant leverage over the kinds of units it ultimately receives.
The phase-out will be gradual rather than abrupt: the cut-off for turnkey applications has been fixed at 31 December 2027.
Thereafter, the emphasis will pivot towards expanding in-house construction by local authorities, approved housing bodies and the Land Development Agency, the State-backed developer.

The move signals a deliberate recalibration of housing policy, prioritising direct delivery over off-the-shelf acquisition. Whether councils possess the capacity to scale up their own building programmes swiftly enough remains to be seen.

The Irish Government intends to discontinue the purchase of so-called turnkey homes by local authorities for social housing, according to a proposal presented to Cabinet on Tuesday by the Minister for Housing, James Browne.

Social housing, which is let at below-market rents to households that cannot afford private accommodation, is provided by local authorities and not-for-profit approved housing bodies. Turnkey purchases have constituted a convenient means of increasing this supply without the authorities bearing construction risk directly.

Turnkey acquisitions involve councils buying newly constructed dwellings from private developers upon completion. Although this mechanism enables tenants to be accommodated relatively rapidly, it has been widely criticised for diminishing the stock of homes available to prospective owner-occupiers.

The Minister has expressed substantial reservations about the practice, arguing that it diverts properties away from the private market. Furthermore, he contends that the State exerts minimal influence over the characteristics of the units it obtains through such transactions.
Nevertheless, the transition will be incremental. Applications for turnkey purchases will remain permissible until 31 December 2027, after which the scheme will be terminated.

Consequently, the delivery of social housing will become increasingly contingent upon direct construction by local authorities, approved housing bodies and the Land Development Agency, a State-owned development body.

This reorientation reflects a broader policy objective of enhancing public control over housing provision. Its ultimate success, however, will depend substantially on whether these bodies can expand their construction capacity sufficiently to offset the loss of turnkey supply.
